headline: Still no run logged since the trail block — absorption has now run several days deeper than a single easy-day reset. Steps stay high; structured work stays fully paused. The first run remains the untaken test.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is unchanged in shape from the last few days but longer in duration: no run, no strength, and an all-day step count that refuses to drop even with formal training on hold. That elevated background load matters — it's real time on feet, not true rest, so "absorption" here means the nervous and structural systems are recovering from the ultra block while the aerobic base keeps ticking over via walking. Strength has now been absent long enough that it's no longer a post-block gap but a standing feature of the log, and the running streak is being carried entirely by the trail days that closed the block rather than anything recent. The four-week running total still towers over the prior block because those back-to-back ultra days sit inside it; that's a load ghost, not current work. The signal to read is not fitness — it's readiness to resume, and none of today's data speaks to that yet because nothing structured was logged.
sections.trends: The 16-week shape is a classic ramp-and-hold: a steep build into the trail crossing followed by a deliberate flat stretch. Against the standing goal of year-round hybrid readiness, that's coherent — a big durability block followed by genuine absorption is exactly the rhythm this athlete has earned the right to run. The year-to-date monthly progression against last year remains dramatic and is the real story of the season; the current pause doesn't dent it. What I'd want to see next is the curve turning back upward with structure, not staying flat by default, because a plateau that extends past absorption stops being recovery and becomes drift.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and the VO2max-adjacent picture are static — the reference point hasn't moved in weeks, and nothing in the recent log could move it, since every trail effort sat deliberately in the lowest zone. That's fine: threshold isn't lost through a controlled ultra block plus a rest window, and the demonstrated speed pedigree in the PB set confirms the high-end engine is intact. But it's now been a long time since anything genuinely tested the top end, so the current threshold figure is increasingly a memory rather than a measurement. Worth re-touching once running resumes.
sections.zones: The recent distribution is almost entirely Zone 1 by design — the trail block was time-on-feet at controlled HR, and the per-session shapes confirm it, with only isolated brief spikes on the longest days. That's the correct intensity signature for what that block was doing. The open question isn't whether the trail work was distributed right — it was — but whether the return reintroduces any real intensity at all, because a resumption that's also all easy running would leave the athlete a long way from their last hard effort.
sections.hr_comparison: The strength HR history shows the expected pattern — moderate averages with brief pushes into the higher zones on the more demanding sessions — but it's all history now, with the most recent strength entries already weeks back. Nothing new to compare on the strength side because nothing new has been logged. On the running side the sources track sensibly across the trail days with no meaningful divergence worth flagging.
sections.calendar: The calendar now shows a clean block of consecutive trail days abruptly giving way to an unbroken run of empty training days. That transition is sharp rather than tapered — the athlete went from maximal to nothing in a single step, which is a legitimate way to close an ultra block but means the resumption will be a genuine restart, not a continuation. The consistency that defined the year is currently on pause, and the calendar's job this week is to show whether the interleaved run/strength cadence reappears or whether running restarts alone.
sections.personal_bests: Nothing in the current pattern points at a PB — the recent work was durability, not speed, and the top-end bests belong to a sharper phase last autumn. They remain realistic targets once structured intensity returns, but that conversation is weeks away, not this week.

watch_items: Watch whether the first logged run returns at a normal easy HR, which would confirm the block absorbed cleanly rather than lingering as fatigue.
Watch whether the resumption reintroduces any real intensity, or whether running restarts entirely easy and leaves the top end untested for even longer.
Watch whether strength re-enters the log at all — its continued absence is now a standing feature, not a post-block gap.
Watch whether the persistently high step count settles once structured training resumes, or holds as a permanent background load worth accounting for.
